Controller code review findings:

1. P0 — `LocalRuntimeAcceptanceAuthority` still has a production initializer default `receiptPersister = { .persisted($0) }`. Any caller that omits the persister can reach `.accepted` after clean cleanup without any durable write. Existing authority tests exercise this bypass. Durable persistence is therefore not a type-level acceptance invariant.

2. P0 — `LocalAcceptanceReceiptStore.writeCanonical` removes `receiptURL` in the atomic-replace failure path. If a valid prior accepted receipt exists and replacement fails, the last-known-good durable evidence can be deleted. A failed replacement must preserve the old receipt and remove only the temporary file.

3. P0 — `isRegularFile` means only `!isDirectory`; it does not verify POSIX regular-file type. FIFO/socket/device nodes can pass the check, after which `Data(contentsOf:)` can become unbounded/blocking. This violates the R12 bounded-load + regular-file-required contract. Use descriptor-based no-follow open/fstat or equivalent strict file-type validation before bounded read.

4. P1 — `loadAccepted` maps any `Data(contentsOf:)` failure to `.notFound`, even after the destination was observed to exist as an admissible path. Permission/I/O races or failures are therefore silently collapsed into absence instead of a bounded fail-closed I/O error. The symlink load test also permits `.malformedJSON` as an alternative to symlink rejection, weakening the claimed symlink invariant.

Required FIX: remove the success-default persister, preserve old receipt on failed replace, enforce actual regular-file + bounded/no-follow read semantics, make existing-file read failure bounded RED, and add mutation/tests that fail if any of those protections are bypassed. Do not edit/repost Worker report 5214729277. No Ready/Merge/Release.
